about: Shared conformance vectors for the decision contract (SDK contract C3). Expectations are stated by hand, never computed from resolve(), so a bug in resolve() cannot make its own vector pass. scope=result vectors are run by the SDK through resolve() AND by each gate through its own code path (BCC: PackPolicy.decide_sync; Shield: PolicyEngine.evaluate_with_basis) with the evaluator's raw result stubbed; scope=resolve vectors cover plumbing a gate reaches without an evaluator result and run through resolve() only. Result encoding: {"$undefined": true} is an evaluator result that was undefined (no rule matched). Changing a vector is a change to the contract surface, not a routine test update.

vectors.name: no_match_takes_the_permit_default

vectors.name: empty_object_is_malformed
vectors.why: Anything the gate cannot interpret fails closed

shield.why: Shield's evaluator entrypoint is the whole data.shield.policy package object, whose display variables (rule_id, name, message) carry Rego defaults, so an object with none of decision/reason_code/controls means no rule matched. Shield therefore takes the event class default for it. Any contract key present is a rule match and goes to resolve() as it is (see the neighbouring vectors).
